sentence: Four-year-old girl who came to the emergency room with a palpable purpuric rash on the lower limbs and buttocks, pain and swelling in the left ankle and the second finger of the right hand.
As background, the week before the start of the clinic she had a case of acute pharyngitis.
Microbiology: rapid detection of group A β-hemolytic streptococcus negative, sterile urine culture, negative blood culture.
Blood count: leukocytes 8320/mm3, hemoglobin 13 g/dl, platelets 276,000/mm3, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) in the first hour of 18 mm/h.

Coagulation tests: prothrombin time 13.9 seconds (range 10-14), Quick index 69% (range 70-150), international normalized ratio (INR) 1.25 (range 0.85-1.15) , activated partial thromboplastin time 31.4 seconds (range 26-36), fibrinogen 429 ng/ml (range 200-400).

Biochemistry: glucose 82 mg/dl, urea 20 mg/dl, creatinine 0.40 mg/dl, total/direct bilirubin 0.4/0.2 mg/dl, total proteins 7.5 g/dl, albumin 3.5 g/dl, total calcium 8.6 mg/dl, GOT/GPT 23/15 IU/l, GGT 15 IU/l, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 254 IU/l, FA 127 IU/l.
Ions: Na 130 mEq/l, K 3.5 mEq/l, Cl 103 mEq/l.
Urine sediment: no proteinuria or significant hematuria is seen.
Due to the clinical characteristics, the case suggests the first possibility of Henoch-Schönlein purpura with joint involvement.
The case progresses satisfactorily with oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and rest.
